summary: Apply PGI analysis, referral mapping and inclusion planning in emergency response. Explore the five-day course and practical outputs.
lede: Gender and inclusion in disaster relief helps practitioners identify unequal risks and access barriers and adapt emergency response plans. Participants practise rapid gender, age and diversity analysis, review sex-, age- and disability-disaggregated data, and develop sector recommendations, safe referral maps and budget-linked actions. Designed for protection, gender and inclusion officers, programme managers and monitoring staff, the course uses practical exercises to support safe consultation, accessible services and follow-up.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for humanitarian and disaster-relief practitioners who assess needs, plan assistance, deliver services or monitor whether affected people can access them safely. It suits staff with operational experience who need to apply protection, gender and inclusion responsibilities across response work.
modules: PGI Rapid Analysis and Risk Priorities
IASC Gender Handbook in Sector Assessment
Protection Referral Mapping and Safe Case Management
prerequisites: Prior experience in humanitarian or disaster-relief assessment, programme planning or assistance delivery is expected. No coding or programming is required.
